what: P1 settle (INTERLOCK 6.2) on gmg r0 (public ep24 boards), our reference poses, FlashCHORD scene on CPU
requested_by: bold-albattani (mesh session), run by a determined-wright helper agent, 2026-10-31 ~21:33-22:15 UTC
machine: this cloud container (Linux, 4 CPU, no GPU); CPU Warp / MuJoCo-Warp; no rental, cost $0

r0.note: <obj>/<obj>.glb is not in git (gitignored); make_assets takes the visual from meshes/library_v3, which does not affect collisions

reference.relation_to_P_sel: object poses = the gmg P_sel tracks (poses.npz sha256 e694dae3..., same file as the r0 manifest p_sim) mapped by table_frame.npz T_table_from_world plus a constant world-z shift per object: +12.904 mm board 1, +10.989 mm board 2 (checked: max residual 0.0 mm, 0.0 deg over 275 frames). Relative pose therefore differs from P_sim by 1.92 mm along world z (board 1 higher), i.e. along the insertion direction.

why: gmg pair key "wooden_piece_1|wooden_piece_2" (report.json pairs) = (target o = host, partner p = guest); their own P1 pre-check used host = wooden_piece_1

our reference: board 2 descends onto board 1 over the run (board 2 lowest point 150 mm at f160 -> 27 mm at f218 while board 1 stays at 26-37 mm); insertion direction d = (0.04, -1.00, -0.05) in board 1 frame = world down at assembly

frames.why: INSERTION run (decisions.json: run 164-274, travel 122 mm, straightness 0.91) -> P1 frame = median frame of the assembled stretch. The gmg assembled stretch on P_sim (= P_sel, flag sim_pose_fallback) is f218-274 (29 frames at stride 2) for both ordered pairs; median = asm[len//2] = 246, the frame the gmg used for P2 and its P1 pre-check. On our reference with the gmg rule (_static_stretches, < 2 mm/frame, >= 5 frames): ordered pair board2<-board1 gives 218-274 (median 246); board1<-board2 splits at 238->240 (2.018 mm/frame vs 1.995 on P_sel, caused by the per-object z shift) -> 240-274, median 258; stride 1 -> 265-274, median 270. Frame 0 is not used: the boards are 30 cm apart there.

deviations: Contact buffers: sim.nconmax=4096, sim.njmax=16384 per world (FlashCHORD SimConfig defaults, configs/sim/replay.yaml) instead of the training config sim=rl (256 / 512). Needed: with 256 / 512 the carved scene overflows the broadphase (MuJoCo-Warp asks for 500-670) and contacts are dropped (asis runs). Buffer size only; 0 overflow lines in every reported run.
17 worlds per env (world 0 nominal, 1..16 jittered) instead of settle_at.py's 1 world; worlds are independent (copies 1 and 7 re-run in 1 world gave identical numbers).

Jitter on both objects' start poses (task instruction; the gmg plain-MuJoCo pre-check jitters the guest only). Draws: default_rng(0).normal((16, 2, 6)), 0.5 mm per axis, 0.005 rad rotation vector per axis, same draws for every configuration (common random numbers).

Drift and tilt are measured from each copy's own start pose (as gmg simphys.settle); drift_vs_ref (from the unjittered pose) is also stored and differs by at most 0.13 cm (the jitter itself). Tilt = full rotation angle of R0^T R1 (gmg convention).
Relative sink is signed (positive = guest moves down relative to the host), as gmg simphys.settle; negative values mean the host dropped further than the guest.

Default control: r0/_default has no inertia.json, so make_assets.py --pieces r0/_default keeps the COM / inertia of the library_v3 mesh surface (COM 3-4 mm from the pieces' solid). Run both: "default" (literal build) and "default_inertia" (exact uniform-solid COM / inertia of the default pieces, scripts/piece_props.py, 0.3 kg).
Snapped variant (snap1, diagnostic only, not the spec): each copy's pair moved rigidly along z so its lowest collision vertex is 1 mm above the table top; relative pose unchanged.
Fall-through: two readings reported (A: clause not applicable; B: conservative).

verdict.reading: P1 as specified FAILS for the carved pieces (mean drift of both boards > 1 cm) and also for the default control (drift and tilt). The drift is the fall of the whole cross: at the assembled frames our reference holds both boards about 3 cm above the table (lowest points 30.7 / 35.0 mm at f246) with no hand within 9 cm, so every copy drops about 3 cm. Tilt, relative sink and NaN pass for the carved pieces; the default fails tilt (13-14 deg host). With the pair lowered rigidly onto the table (diagnostic, not the spec) the carved pieces pass every numeric P1 criterion at f246, f258 and f270 and the default fails tilt. With the training sim config buffers (nconmax 256, njmax 512; settle_at.py as is, 1 world) the carved scene overflows the broadphase in 16/16 copies and both boards fall through the table; the default does not overflow.
